clues: This city sits on the south shore of a wide bay, in the south west of a far north island. Steam rises from hot springs in the land around it.
In summer the sun here hardly sets for weeks on end. In mid winter the whole day lasts less than five hours.
In 1845 the nation's old assembly came back to this town and set up there. That move in effect made the town the capital of the island.
No capital city of a free land sits farther north than this one. It is the topmost capital in the whole world.
The president of Iceland works from this city. His office was set here in 1944, when the land first had a president.
